name: Indiana Limestone
spec: ASTM C568 Class II Medium Density (Salem limestone). Compressive strength 4,000–8,000 psi. Quarried, sawn, and detailed in twelve-inch ashlar courses; load-bearing on a poured concrete base.
patina: Develops a soft grey-buff weather skin over the first decade. Stains can be poulticed by any mason; cracks can be repaired by re-cutting and re-bedding a single block.

name: White Oak (rift sawn)
spec: Rift-sawn quartersawn white oak (Quercus alba), kiln-dried to 8% MC, finished with hard-wax oil (Osmo Polyx). 1¼-inch flooring, solid 4×4 furniture stock, custom millwork. No engineered substitutes.
patina: Darkens slightly under wax over the first two years; thereafter stable. Dings and scratches sand out in fifteen minutes. Refinishable indefinitely.

name: Brass (sand-cast)
origin: Sand-cast in Pennsylvania foundry; tubing extruded in Connecticut
spec: C36000 free-machining brass for fittings; C26000 cartridge brass for sheet and tubing. Unlacquered; allowed to develop patina. Plumbing fittings sized to NSF/ANSI 61.
patina: Polishes mirror-bright; darkens in handling to a deep amber. We do not polish. Re-cast or re-drawn from scrap by any foundry; cost recovers most of the metal.

name: Lime Plaster (NHL 3.5)
spec: Three-coat NHL 3.5 hydraulic lime plaster on metal lath. Final coat tinted with raw umber pigment. Vapor-permeable; no acrylic additives. Self-healing micro-cracks via ongoing carbonation.
patina: The wall absorbs and releases moisture; this is the point. A new patch is invisible after a season's exposure. No paint. No primer. No drywall.

name: Terrazzo (marble chip)
origin: Carrara marble chip, Vermont mill base, poured in place
spec: Cement-based terrazzo, 75% white Carrara chip / 25% Verde Alpi, 1¾-inch slab on a divided substrate. Honed finish. Brass divider strips at expansion joints.
patina: Spalls can be re-poured locally. The floor is the building's heaviest single element and its quietest one. Sealed once a decade.

name: Belgian Linen
spec: 100% Belgian flax, woven 240 g/m² for curtains, 165 g/m² for bedding. Stone-washed, undyed. Replaced as needed; the building stocks bolts of identical cloth in the basement.
patina: Softens with each wash. After thirty years a curtain is not the same curtain. Threadbare panels are cut down to towels, then to rags, then composted. Nothing is thrown out.
